trimmingSuggestions.description: While Dr. Russell's acknowledgement of individual project challenges is valid, trimming this brief segment could streamline the video and maintain a higher level of dynamism.
Dr. McMullin's detailed explanation of prototypes and reliance on previous observations, while informative, could be slightly condensed to enhance the overall pace.

text_to_speech: The system CDR is basically the overall view of the design aspects and so it has been a six year process to get to this stage and so hundreds of engineers and scientists from around the world from the member country institutions have participated I was involved with ALMA and now at ESO with ELT so it's about the same scale size of complexity - each project is different of course and comes with different challenges I think that that's one of the attractions for astronomers and engineers, is working out how to overcome these challenges and I think they've really got the right team in place to do that, there are a lot of experts on board and people are so eager to actually make the SKA the best telescope it can be. Sets of the requirements are quite challenging technically and so finding designs that can actually fulfill that performance are difficult and so we've gone through a number different prototyping stages some of them were not successful but that's the reason you go into this you learn a lot about the designs their practicality and you refine that. There are lots of precursor observatories that we're benefiting from, there are other observatories around the world that are large facilities like the SKA but in terms of the overall scale of the project and its audacity and trying to address all these different facets it really is unprecedented. The SKA is going to be one of the major observatories for the future it'll be so complementary to the other great observatories that will be around: the JWST, ALMA itself, the ELT telescopes in the optical and infrared The team has really been outstanding and I speak not only of the team here at the headquarters but also the broader team from our member institutions that were so supportive throughout If you look at what's been achieved in the last few years it's really quite a remarkable - this year in particular has been a huge push with the creation of the IGO, the design really coming to maturity. Certainly looking from the outside it's very very impressive. They've done a tremendous job of actually getting the consortia to the point where they're able to just to move forward with the actual construction Having this milestone of the system CDR is really the foundation for everything in 2020 - this is the year where we have to pull together the construction proposal itself It's just so exciting that right now it's actually all coming together to the point where it's a tangible project it looks like a telescope now We've gotten our wish we get to continue to move forward on the project and it is fantastically exciting to really see this Observatory beginning to come together transitioning over the next year from the analysis and documentation exercise that all the planning is intact to the actual execution and that's fantastic

youtube_description:
Great news to mark the end of 2019: the SKA has passed a major engineering milestone after a positive overall design, costing & planning review by independent experts from major astronomical facilities, bringing to a close six years of hard work by hundreds of engineers and scientists in more than 20 countries around the world. The next task will be to put together the SKA’s construction proposal in 2020! 

Find out more about this major step here:
youtube_title: Designing the SKA - experts endorse the telescope's overall design!
